text: Let's combine tables the KQL way — joins.
Join kind equals left outer is exactly Databricks Lesson 55's left join — every left row kept, matched or not, unmatched columns coming back null. Same core kinds, KQL's own syntax.

And dollar sign left and dollar sign right resolve a column that exists on both sides — the exact same problem trips dot vendor I-D versus zones dot vendor I-D solved before, just written differently.

But here's the real caveat — joining a stream against a small, static lookup table is cheap. Joining two large, fast-moving streams together is genuinely harder — you have to decide how long to wait for a late match before giving up.
Same join concepts, a real new complication once both sides are moving. Next lesson: KQL's time series functions, bin and its real relatives.
